items.author: sylvadragon.bsky.social
items.context: Organised chaos then? lol. 😂 It's better than what I have, a few cupboards full to overflowing with old pc games, dvds, lightbulbs and all kinds of other stuff. then plastic crates with plushies on top.
items.text: A cupboard full of old PC games sounds like a treasure chest. If any of them won't run on a modern PC, GOG sells many classics with the fixes already included.

items.author: klneidecker.com
items.context: Hell yeah. DOS. NES. Infocom, Interplay, Binary Systems, Looking Glass Software. Anyone who can make quality games that don’t need a graphics card that either A) costs $1800 now because reasons or B) can’t be bought because no stock, will fill a niche and be rewarded.
items.text: Old DOS games prove it. GOG sells many of them DRM-free, already set up to run on a modern PC, so they just work.

items.author: priscillakim.bsky.social
items.context: "When was the first time you killed a man?" *slow drag on cigarette, distant look in eyes* "... it was the days of DOS text parser adventure games. King's Quest 2. The church." "No. You typed...?" "Yes. 'kill monk'."
items.text: Peak parser era. Half the fun was discovering which words the game would actually accept.
